The exact weighted periodization/recovery kernels are the supplied unassigned cutoff-factorization identities at that kappa, with the stated unitary c_d cancellation and no additional factor. Dilation of the fixed profile and Peetre for either sign of r give the kernel majorant C_r rho^(d/2) F_r(k-rho xi). The report explicitly uses rho>=1 to ensure constants in the bracket comparison are fixed-profile/r/d dependent. Its xi integral has Jacobian rho^-d, giving rho^-d/2, whereas the shifted integer-lattice sum has spacing1 and gives rho^d/2; their PRODUCT is radius-independent before Schur square root. Density/distributional recovery includes all real r and does not sample rough Fourier data. Every new explanatory sentence agrees with this derivation.

The full-domain recovery factorization with chi_rho psi_rho=chi_rho and Bessel isometries is explicit, including negative sigma. The torus inclusion has diagonal <k/rho>^-gamma; the unit-cube Peetre comparison at u=q gamma>d gives the displayed locally integrable weight integral and rho^d volume factor. Finite-rank j-1 truncations transfer each diagonal singular value by bounded outer factors, proving compactness and summable qth powers; taking the qth root gives rho^(d/q). The report independently checks direct-sum qth powers for the two phase blocks and the unitary input/output swap. Constants may depend on the deterministic Schatten index q; the later probability proof freezes Q before varying its moment index. No projection/self-adjoint cutoff assumption or Hilbert-Schmidt endpoint is introduced. The new volume-comparison gloss is correct.

The physical mask remains eta(x/R)^2 while both envelope localizations use chi_rho. The named unassigned two-variance/driver hypotheses supply an R,N,I-uniform variance budget with the same eta^2 base; the finite Gaussian bound is applied at even q>=Q with q gamma>d. Unnormalized Schatten monotonicity bounds the q norm by the FIXED Q norm, retaining R^(d/Q) with a constant independent of later q. Coarse unit partitions, zero-initial continuous paths and C^eta_t→C^theta produce the finite-sum path bound. The fixed-R Lq limit preserves the estimate without radius-uniform construction convergence, and a controlled larger even q gives sqrt(v) for arbitrary finite v>=1. No F-column estimate follows.
